<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par164 />''and when thou dost overtake them'' (as soon as thou shalt have overtaken), ''thou shalt say unto them''. Naturally, examples of this kind are very closely related to conditional sentences; see, therefore, the examples in {{GHGpar|112|kk}} and {{GHGpar|159|g}}. On the connexion of an imperfect consecutive or a perfect with detached expressions of time (as equivalent to complete clauses), cf. {{GHGpar|111|b}}; on the imperfect consecutive after {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}} and a statement of time, cf. {{GHGpar|111|g}}; on the perfect consecutive following a detached statement of time, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=6}}, cf. {{GHGpar|112|oo}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=29|verse=10}} an imperative with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} follows the perfect consecutive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|164|c}}
(5) The fact that one action or event has not yet taken place on the occurrence of another, is expressed by {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם}} (an adverb, not a conjunction) with the imperfect (according to {{GHGpar|107|c}}). The apodosis, which may consist of a subject and perfect or even of a noun-clause ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=15}}),<ref>On the perfect in the protasis, which is critically doubtful, cf. {{GHGpar|107|c}}.</ref> is then connected by {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} (or {{GHGheb|text=וְהִנֵּה}}) as in the examples above, under no. 3, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=4}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=8}}) {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם יִשְׁכָּ֫בוּ וְאַנְשֵׁי הָעִיר ... נָסַ֫בּוּ וג׳|translate=they had not yet lain down, and}} (=when) ''the men of the city'' ... ''compassed'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=25}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|164|d}}
'''2.''' Conjunctions used to introduce temporal clauses are {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} (with perfect, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=12}}; with imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=41|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=21|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=31|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=19|hidebook=1}}) and {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} as an original demonstrative, cf. {{GHGpar|138|a}}; hence {{GHGheb|text=עַד־אֲשֶׁר נָשׁוּב}} is properly ''up to that'' (moment)—''we shall return''.</ref> ''when'' ({{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} with the imperfect also=''as often as'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=8|verse=4}}; with perfect {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=5}}); less frequently {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}<ref>Cf. the frequent use of ''wenn'' [prop. ''if''] for ''wann'' [=''when''] in German.</ref> (joined with a perfect), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=41|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=13}}=''quotiescunque''; also in the same sense with an imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=36|verse=4}}; with a perfect, equivalent to the ''futurum exactum'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=4|verse=4}}. Other conjunctions of time are the compounds {{GHGheb|text=כְּמוֹ|translate=when}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=כַּֽאֲשֶׁר|translate=when, after that}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַד־אֲשֶׁר}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַד־כִּי|translate=until}} (also the simple {{GHGheb|text=עַד־}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=22}} [with the imperfect=''only when'', as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=10|verse=5}}]); 2:5, &c.; especially in the formula {{GHGheb|text=עַד־בִּלְתִּי הִשְׁאִיר לוֹ|translate=until there was none left remaining to him}} (where indeed it would be very natural to read {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁאִיר}} the infin. constr., as elsewhere after {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי}}, {{GHGpar|114|s}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=11|verse=8|hidebook=1}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=19}} ''while, as long as''); {{GHGheb|text=עַד אֲשֶׁר לֹא|translate=before that}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=1}}, 2, 6 with an imperfect, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=עַד}} with a perfect; {{GHGheb|text=עַד־אִם}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַר־אֲשֶׁר אִם|translate=until the time when}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרֵֽי־אֲשֶׁר}} (for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=אַחַר־אֲשֶׁר}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=48}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=9}} simply {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרֵי}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=7}} simply {{GHGheb|text=אַחַר}}) ''after that''; {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָז}} (prop. ''since that time''; the dependent clause is attached to it in the same way as the attributive clause to the demonstrative {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGpar|138|e}}) ''since'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּטֶ֫רֶם}} (and simply {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם}} {{GHGpar|107|c}}) ''before''; {{GHGheb|text=קַדְמַת}} (for {{GHGheb|text=קַדְמַת אֲשֶׁר}}) ''before'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=129|verse=6}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|164|e}}
Rem. 1. With regard to the tenses used with the above conjunctions, the rules are practically the same as those given in {{GHGpar|158|d}} for causal clauses.
